exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, established on localizer Runway zero sev-en left, three thousand feet.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reports established on the localizer at the cleared platform altitude, awaiting the descent clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Director, maintain three thousand feet until glide path interception, cleared ILS Runway zero sev-en left approach.
exchanges.meaning: ATC issues the mandatory level constraint until vertical capture and clears the ILS approach.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Maintain three thousand feet until glide path interception, cleared ILS Runway zero sev-en left approach, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back the altitude constraint and approach clearance verbatim — descending early here is the hearback trap.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, confirm glide path intercepted.
exchanges.meaning: Controller's confirmation query verifying vertical glide path capture.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, glide path intercepted, descending on glide path.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot confirms the glide path is captured and the aircraft is now descending on profile.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, contact Hong Kong Tower wun wun eight day-see-mal sev-en.
exchanges.meaning: Handoff to Tower frequency 118.7 after glide path capture is confirmed.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Tower wun wun eight day-see-mal sev-en, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Brief readback of the frequency transfer to Tower.

vocabulary.definition: Clearance authorizing localizer tracking and glideslope descent; descent is authorized only once the glide path is intercepted — being established on the localizer alone does NOT permit descent.
Mandatory level constraint: the aircraft must not descend below the cleared platform altitude (e.g. 3,000 ft) until the glideslope diamond centers.
Pilot confirmation of vertical glide path capture — the aircraft is now descending on profile.
Standard ILS descent angle: about 300 ft per nautical mile; rate of descent ≈ ground speed × 5 (e.g. 140 kt → 700 ft/min).
Spurious ground-reflection lobes radiated at 6° and 9°; capturing one from above can command a lethal 1,500+ ft/min dive — always intercept the glide path from below.
UHF transmitter (329.15–335.00 MHz) adjacent to the runway touchdown zone (~1,000 ft past threshold), projecting overlapping 90 Hz (upper) and 150 Hz (lower) lobes to form the 3.0° electronic ramp.

Marked by double yellow lines with alternating yellow ladders on taxiways; a taxiing aircraft crossing them in low visibility (CAT II/III) can reflect and bend the glideslope signal for an aircraft on final.

quiz.question: On a standard 3-degree ILS glide path with a ground speed of 140 knots, what is the required rate of descent to remain on the glide path centerline?
quiz.explanation: Standard 3° glideslope rule of thumb: Ground Speed * 5 = Rate of Descent. 140 * 5 = 700 ft/min.

quiz.question: Why is it hazardous to attempt capturing an ILS glide path from above the published glide slope angle?
options: Ground reflections generate false glide path lobes at odd multiples (e.g. 6 degrees), which can cause the flight director/autopilot to command dangerously excessive descent rates.
It causes the transponder to squawk 7600.
It permanently damages the aircraft's glideslope receiver antenna.
It invalidates the aircraft's altimeter calibration.
quiz.explanation: UHF ground reflections create false glideslope signals at steep angles (typically 6° and 9°). Intercepting from above risks capturing a 6° false slope requiring a lethal 1,500+ ft/min descent rate.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Phonetic Guide | Operational Example |
|---|---|
| Cleared ILS Runway [num] | Clearance authorizing localizer tracking and glideslope descent. | kleerd eye-el-ess... | "Cleared ILS Runway 07L approach." |
| Maintain [alt] until glide path | Mandatory level constraint until vertical capture point. | mayn-TAYN... un-TIL GLYDE-path | Must not descend until diamond centers! |
| Glide path intercepted | Pilot confirmation of vertical glide path capture. | GLYDE-path in-ter-SEP-ted | Confirms aircraft is descending on profile. |
| 3-degree descent gradient | Standard descent angle: ~300 ft per nautical mile. | TREE de-GREE de-SENT | ROD = Ground Speed * 5 (e.g. 700 ft/min). |
| False glideslope lobe | Spurious ground reflection lobes radiated at 6° and 9°. | fawls GLYDE-slope | Dangerous if captured from above! |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- Day 31 Review (+1d): Localizer full-scale deflection is only ±2.5 degrees. Always report "Established localizer" to trigger Tower frequency transfer.
- Day 30 Review (+2d): Universal intermediate approach speed is 160 knots to 4 DME. Approach must be fully stabilized by 1,000 ft in IMC.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — ILS Critical & Sensitive Areas
sections.body: Have you ever noticed the double yellow lines on airport taxiways with alternating yellow ladders? Those mark the ILS Critical Area! If a taxiing aircraft crosses those lines while another aircraft is landing in low visibility (CAT II/III), its metal fuselage will reflect and bend the glideslope signal, causing the landing plane's autopilot to follow a warped signal straight into the ground!
